source.title: Data from USDA ARS Central Plains Experimental Range (CPER) near Nunn, CO: Cattle weight gains managed with light, moderate and heavy grazing intensities
source.rowUnit: one animal per grazing year/pasture, with entry and exit weights
source.studyDescription: British- and continental-breed yearling cattle under light, moderate or heavy grazing; one remaining pasture replicate per treatment.

units.initialWeight: kg, converted from published lb using 0.45359237 kg/lb
units.observedShrunkAdg: kg/head/day, published ADG_shrunk converted from lb/head/day

limitations: Only one pasture replication per grazing-intensity treatment remains; do not interpret treatment differences causally.
Rows are one animal-season each, and ear-tag identifiers may be reused between years; the stable evaluation key is year, pasture, type, owner, tag color and tag.
This file contains individual entry/exit weights, not a daily or 28-day weight series, individual DMI, or initial pasture biomass.

The source documents changes in weighing and shrink protocols over time. Raw endpoint ADG is derived for a transparent weight-scale comparison; the published shrunk ADG is also preserved for sensitivity.
The dataset covers CPER yearlings in grazing seasons and does not validate the full engine, costs, DMI, or a pasture-versus-confinement counterfactual.
